newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK-LANGUAGE TEMPO/NEWSWEEK TO HIT STANDS IN MAY.
newsitem.headline: GREEK-LANGUAGE TEMPO/NEWSWEEK TO HIT STANDS IN MAY.

text.p: Newsweek magazine and Athens-based New Communications SA will be publishing a Greek language newsweekly, Tempo/Newsweek, Newsweek said on Monday.
The premiere issue of Tempo/Newsweek is scheduled to hit the stands in the second week of May.

"In creating this first modern Greek news magazine, we aspire to provide Greek readers with the high quality reporting, writing and photography offered by news magazines worldwide," said editor-in-chief Theodore Kaloudis.
The magazine will be published in Athens by Newcom and draw on the editorial and reporting provided by Newsweek's international network of bureaus for about 35 percent of the content.
The remaining 65 percent will be produced by Tempo/Newsweek's staff of 55 journalists.

"It's a new variety of magazine on the Greek market, designed by Greek journalists aiming to cover subjects of interest including politics, economics, society, culture, science and technology," said Kaloudis.
Newsweek has a growing worldwide audience of nearly 24 million and now publishes three English language international editions with a combined circulation of about 725,00 copies weekly, it said.

"We consider Greece an important market and are pleased that Tempo/Newsweek is the newest member of a rapidly developing network of news magazines worlwide," said Newsweek International president Peter Luffman. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
